rubric: Designed effect (weight 1): the property the verb is defined to change - open/close: isOpen; activate/deactivate: isActivated; move/pick up: location of the moved object; pour: contents of the poured container and presence of each poured substance; mix: presence of each substance in the mixed container; use lighter on X: X hasCombusted, isCombusting and present; eat X: X present; connect A to B: connectedTo of both terminals; teleport: agent location.

Practical consequence (weight 1): temperature (and, for liquids, state of matter) of objects placed into, or exposed by opening/activating, a heating or cooling container or device; contents of containers inside an activated water source.
Recorded only (weight 0): containers whose contents change as a side effect (destination of a pour, container of an eaten object, a mixed container's contents).
Identity: every property refers to the S0 object; objects created by the action cannot be declared. Choose roles that name exactly one S0 object.
Never consult restoration results, recovery paths or another declaration.
ambiguities: Should temperature changes caused by a thermal device count as a practical consequence (R2) when they are small over one tick?
For combustion, is the object's eventual deletion ('present') part of the designed effect (R1) or only recorded (R3)?
For pour/mix, is the container's 'contents' the designed effect or are the substances' identities ('present')?
Is the location of objects inside a container that is opened/closed relevant?
For electrical connections, should both terminals or only the first be declared?
Which recorded side effects (R3) to list at all.
note: rule-based technical comparison; NOT inter-annotator agreement
